title: Buying a five-dollar Albert clarinet and first lessons with Chaligny
summary: In 1923 he bought a B-flat Albert clarinet with his five-dollar Christmas savings, taught himself hymns, then took lessons from Old Man Chaligny.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Well, it was, let me see, let me see. It was a little different in a way, but I tell you bands like Rene Punch, Buddy Petit, while they were playing the music almost similar to what we're playing now. Oh yeah. Yes. And sometime it'll be better. Yeah. Because them boys, they just was gifted and they really knew what they were doing. They just was gifted. I don't think they knew a bit of music. If they did, I didn't know anything about it. They had a good head for it. You see. Yeah. When did you start to learn and study music? Oh, well, I'll tell you when I first began music in 1923. I was a white gentleman living across from the Arcade Theater. So, someone told me he had a clarinet for sale. So, they knew I wanted to, you know, I used to try to beat the drum, I used to sing. They knew I would, had liked music. So, they told me about this gentleman. So, I went to see him about it. So, he said, yeah, he was selling me the clarinet. He wanted $5 for it. He said, he let me have it for $5. And so, guess how I got the money? I had a Christmas saving that year. The bank right there on Sedan and Cleveland. It used to be a bank there. And I saved up that whole year. And guess how much it was that I saved? $5 that whole year. Christmas saving. So, I taken that $5 check and brought it right to him and got this client. It was an Albert system. Albert system. Yeah, B-flat clarinet. And so, from that I start making noise around the house, trying to learn how to blow it. My mother would run out with all that noise. And, Thomas, get out of here. She used to call me Brother. My nickname was Brother. I said, Brother, get out of here with all that noise. I'd go out in the backyard. We had a large backyard. I'd go in the yard and try to blow it again. So, finally I find myself playing Hum, Sweet Hum, Nearer, My God, The D. And a few other numbers like that. So, the boy said, Brother, why don't you go take some lessons? Say, you did all that much by yourself. You take a lesson, you know, give you more ideas. So, I decided to take a lesson. So, I went to Chalini. Old man Chalini. He was living on St. Claude, between Domaine and St. Philip. I went there and he started giving me lessons. A, B, C, D, R, A, Mi, Fa, Son, that's it. About how old were you then? Well, it was in 24 then. 1924. You see? So, that make I was about... 22 years old. 23 years old. That's it. Yes. I was about 23 years old. And, so I got to... Did he use a book?
